fields.reasoning: The gate step runs its commands with sh -c in the run worktree (stepRunner.CommandOutput), so rhiza there is the installed binary, while the step's environment already carries the workflow's [env] (stepEnv), SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA included. conductor-land-render-head-build solved the same problem for land and render inside the operations with runViaHead, and ship open-pr's pre-push check builds the head for its check (prePushHeadCheck). Changing the builtin's gate command to a shell fallback such as ${SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA:-rhiza} would skip the on-demand build (shipHeadBuild) and put Rhiza-repo knowledge into the generic builtin. Redirecting inside runCheck itself would also redirect the pre-push check's in-process call in its temporary checkout, which already has its own head path, so the redirect goes at the operation's entry.
fields.statement: rhiza check itself runs through the run's head build, as rhiza land and rhiza render already do (runViaHead): when the environment names SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA and it is not the running binary, the check operation execs that build's check --json in the same directory with the request's flags (--base, --skip-reference, --branch-newer-format) and reports its result. The builtin ship-change gate's commands stay as they are (plain rhiza check), so every workflow whose [env] names a head build gets it with no workflow change. Only the check operation (CLI and api call) does this; the in-process callers of runCheck (the pre-push check, run code-check, health) keep their own behaviour.

fields.reasoning: The orchestrator's hint asks for a fallback to the installed rhiza only when no head build exists. Land and render already treat a named-but-unbuildable head as an error (conductor-land-render-head-build), and checking with the installed binary in that case would bring back exactly the false docs/reference failures this change set fixes, or worse a false pass. shipRunHead returns an error on any non-zero exit, but check exits 1 on findings, so the report must be parsed from the child's stdout as prePushHeadCheck does.
fields.statement: rhiza check falls back to the running (installed) rhiza only when no head build is named: SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA unset, or naming the running binary. A named head that is missing is built on demand under SHIP_HEAD_BUILD (shipHeadBuild); a missing head with SHIP_HEAD_BUILD empty, a failed build, or a head whose output is not a check report fails the check with an error naming the head build, never a silent in-process check. A head report with failing findings exits non-zero, so check reads its --json report even when the child exits non-zero and reports those findings with check's usual exit.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestCheckHeadBuild shows, with SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA naming a fake head that records its argv: rhiza check invoking it as check --json with --base, --skip-reference and --branch-newer-format passed through when set, and returning the fake's report, an ok one and one with a fail finding that the fake prints while exiting 1; with SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA unset, or naming the running binary, check running in-process with no exec; with the head missing and SHIP_HEAD_BUILD set, the build running first; with it missing and SHIP_HEAD_BUILD empty, or the fake printing no report, check failing with an error naming the head build; and runCheck called directly (as the pre-push check and run code-check call it) running in-process with SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA set. go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/ship-gate-head-check$' passes a new testscript: a repo whose docs/reference was written by rhiza docs and then edited to document a CLI flag this build does not have (a branch that adds the flag), where plain rhiza check fails on the generated-reference comparison; a workflow run whose gate step runs rhiza check, with SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA naming a fake head build that logs its argv and prints an ok check report, passes the gate and the log shows check --json; the same run with SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA unset fails the gate on command 1 rhiza check. go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestLandRenderHeadBuild|TestShipHeadBuildOnDemand|TestPrePush' still passes, and make self-check passes. Touches internal/api/check.go, internal/api/ship_build.go, internal/api/ship_build_test.go, cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/ship-gate-head-check.txtar and .rhiza/workflows/ship-rhiza.toml.
fields.statement: In a run whose environment names SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA, rhiza check (the CLI and api call check) runs the PR head's build instead of checking in-process: it gets the binary from shipHeadBuild (built on demand under SHIP_HEAD_BUILD) and execs its check --json in the same directory with the request's --base, --skip-reference and --branch-newer-format, unless the running binary is that build, and reports the child's check report (read from its stdout even when it exits non-zero on failing findings) with check's usual output and exit; so the conductor default's gate step (plain rhiza check) judges docs/reference and the docs-command rule by the branch's own registry, and a change set that adds a CLI command, flag or setting no longer fails the gate and hands back to conduct in a loop. With SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA unset, or naming the running binary, check runs in-process as today; a missing head with SHIP_HEAD_BUILD empty, a failed build, or output that is no check report fails with an error naming the head build. The pre-push check, run code-check and health keep calling runCheck in-process. .rhiza/workflows/ship-rhiza.toml's comment says the head build serves check as well as land and render.
